'''John Cameron Semple''' (born 1947) is a [[botanist]], [[Cytotaxonomy|cytotaxonomist]], [[professor emeritus]], and [[adjunct professor]] at the [[University of Waterloo]] in Ontario, Canada.{{Sfn|Semple|2021b}} He was born in [[Boston]] and earned a degree of [[Bachelor of Science]] in 1969 from [[Tufts University]], followed in 1971 and 1972 by [[Master of Arts]] and [[Doctor of Philosophy]] degrees from [[Washington University in St. Louis]]. Semple is known for his work with members of the tribe [[Astereae]], particularly [[goldenrods]], [[List of Aster synonyms|American asters]], and [[Golden aster|goldenasters]],{{Sfn|Semple|2021e}} and he maintains the University of Waterloo Astereae Lab website.{{Sfn|Semple|2021b}} Semple's wife is Brenda, and in 2013, he named a newly discovered goldenrod species ''[[Solidago brendiae]]'' in honor of her.{{Sfn|Semple|2013a|p=4}}

==Early life and education==
John Cameron Semple was born in 1947{{Sfn|IPNI|2020}} in Boston, the second child of three to Bob Semple, an accountant, and Margaret Semple, a school teacher. As a child, John had an interest in art and took classes in the subject at a local museum. In high school, he became interested in biology, and this led him to enroll in [[Tufts University]] in 1965 to begin the study of medicine. At the encouragement of a botany professor he met at Tufts, he included courses in botany and taxonomy in his studies and decided to attend graduate school to become a botanist.{{Sfn|Lotosky|2012}}

After earning a [[Bachelor of Science]] in 1969 from Tufts,{{Sfn|Botanical Society of America|1995}} Semple enrolled at [[Washington University in St. Louis]], spending most of his time at the [[Missouri Botanical Garden]].{{Sfn|Lotosky|2012}} In 1971 and 1972, he earned [[Master of Arts]] and [[Doctor of Philosophy]] degrees in biology with a focus on botany.{{Sfn|Botanical Society of America|1995}} His 1972 PhD dissertation was entitled ''The Cytology, Flavonoid Chemistry and Systematics of the Texas Sleepy Daisy ''Xanthisma texanum'' DC. (Asteraceae)''.{{Sfn|Semple|2021b}} Semple acquired a background in cytotaxonomy and evolutionary classification while performing this research, as well as an affinity toward the study of flowering plants in the family [[Asteraceae]].{{Sfn|Lotosky|2012}}

==Career==
For post-doctoral studies, Semple remained at Washington University in St. Louis, also serving as a lecturer and visiting assistant professor, into the summer of 1974. Beginning that fall, he became a lecturer at the [[University of Waterloo]], Ontario, Canada, where he spent his career and retired in 2012.{{Sfn|Lotosky|2012}} One of Semple's early notable doctoral students was Canadian botanist [[Luc Brouillet]].{{Sfn|Semple|Brouillet|1980a}}{{Sfn|Semple|Brouillet|1980b}}

The majority of Semple's post-retirement work has been focused on the goldenrod genus ''[[Solidago]]''.{{Sfn|Semple|2021c}} In February 2021, he and botanist [[James B. Beck (botanist)|James B. Beck]] published a revision of the genus based on a large [[Phylogenomics|phylogenomic]] study. This revision can be viewed on Semple's website{{Sfn|Semple|2021d}} as well as in the original paper.{{Sfn|Semple|Beck|2021a}}

===Awards===
Semple received the COSEWIC Service Award from the [[Committee on the Status of Endangered Wildlife in Canada]] in 1998, and the [[John Goldie Award]] from the Field Botanists of Ontario in 2018.{{Sfn|Semple|n.d.a}}

==Personal life==
Semple and his wife Brenda have three sons and several grandchildren.{{Sfn|Lotosky|2012}}
